# Authoring HTML pages (the "HTML pages" visual tier)

Each `html` scene is one designed full-screen page (1920×1080) you author at
`<out_dir>/pages/scene_NN.html`, rendered by headless Chrome. The page is screenshotted at
progress `p=0..1`; `seek.js` freezes its CSS reveals so the entrance animates then holds.

## Boilerplate (link the bundled design system)
```html
<!doctype html><html><head><meta charset="utf-8">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="file:///ABS/PATH/TO/skill/assets/html/base.css">
<!-- theme.css lives at <out_dir>/theme.css — generated by scripts/theme.py, NOT in the skill assets dir -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="file:///ABS/OUT_DIR/theme.css">
<!-- motifs.css is in the skill assets dir -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="file:///ABS/PATH/TO/skill/assets/html/motifs.css">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="stage"><!-- your layout --></div>
  <script src="file:///ABS/PATH/TO/skill/assets/html/seek.js"></script>
</body></html>
```
Use absolute `file://` paths. Order: `base.css` → `theme.css` (from `<out_dir>`) → `motifs.css` (from `assets/html/`).

## Form selection — choose the form the CONTENT wants (do NOT default to a card grid)
**Design is choosing, not matching.** A `.card`/`.row` grid is the right answer ONLY for **parallel,
unordered, equal-weight** items. The moment the content has **order, magnitude, a relationship, time,
or two axes**, a non-card form says it better. For each beat, name the 2–3 forms it *could* take, then
pick the one whose shape matches the content (all classes are in `base.css`, all reveal-ready):

| The content is… | Reach for |
|---|---|
| **A few standout numbers / KPIs** | `.scorecard` (3 `.tile`: big `.num` + `.lab`, optional `.delta up/down`) — or one hero `.stat` + `.unit` when a single number IS the point |
| **A process / sequence / steps** | `.flow` (`.step` = `.n`/`.t`/`.s`, `.arrow` between) — or `.timeline` if the steps are dated or one is the focus (`.tl-node.on`) |
| **A relationship / structure** (inputs→decision, centre+peers) | `.hubspoke` (`.hs-spoke` × N → `.hs-connect` → `.hs-hub`) |
| **Two axes / a positioning** | `.quadrant` (2×2 `.cell`, focal `.cell.on`, `.ax-x`/`.ax-y` labels) |
| **Parts of a whole / a share** | `.segbar` (100% stacked `.seg`, widths inline) or `.meter` (`.fill` width inline) |
| **A comparison** (A vs B, before→after) | a `.compare` split (`.defocus` the non-focal side); `.quadrant` if two real axes |
| **One idea / a verbatim line** | `.pullquote` (+ `<cite>`) — or a single hero `.stat` |
| **Colour-coded categories** (bold, scannable) | `.blocks two` / `.blocks three` — one hue per `.block` from the THEME: `var(--accent)`, `var(--accent2)`, and for a 3rd either `var(--green)` (a theme-neutral alias) or a `color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent) 55%,var(--accent2))`; verify the 3rd doesn't clash — if you need 3 strongly-distinct on-brand hues and the theme only has 2, use `.blocks two` or `cards` instead. Never grey filler, never a raw hex. |
| **A decomposition** (165 = 123 + 42) | a `.grid` of labeled `.bar` rows (widths inline) or a `.segbar` |
| **Truly parallel, equal-weight items** | a `.card` grid (`.dash` 3-up / `.grid-asym`) — the *considered* choice for THIS shape only |
| **A title / section** | `.kicker` + `.rule` + `.title` (+ `.sub`); a mono `.chrome` footer ties the deck together |

For each beat, record the pick as a one-line **form ledger**: *winner — beats `<runner-up>` because …*
(the content-planner emits this; the critic audits it).

## Reveal animation (so the page captures cleanly)
- Add `class="reveal"` or `class="reveal-up"` to elements you want to animate in.
- Stagger by giving later elements an inline positive delay: `style="animation-delay:.18s"`.
- ONLY use CSS animations via these classes. **No** `setTimeout`/JS-driven motion, **no** external
  network assets (images/fonts/CDNs) — they break deterministic, offline, seekable capture.

## Faithfulness (required)
Every number, name, date, and claim on the page must come from the material (or a verified
source) — type the real data into the HTML. Never invent figures or labels. Data lives on the
page as real text/bars, not as a decorative picture. The critic checks the page against the
narration (R2 audio↔visual) and the facts (R1d/R1e).

## Example (a faithful breakdown page)
```html
<div class="stage">
  <div class="kicker reveal">2025 · 165 次发射</div>
  <div class="rule reveal" style="animation-delay:.05s"></div>
  <div class="title reveal-up" style="animation-delay:.1s">真正能争夺的，只有一小块</div>
  <div class="grid" style="margin-top:40px">
    <div class="bar reveal-up" style="animation-delay:.25s;width:74%;background:var(--blue)">自用 Starlink · 123</div>
    <div class="bar reveal-up" style="animation-delay:.4s;width:26%;background:var(--orange)">对外发射 · 42</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Motifs & pictures (make pages fancier)

Also link `assets/html/motifs.css` (after `base.css`). Motifs are **atmosphere behind real
content** — they assert no fact, so they stay decorative; the real data is the text/bars.

**CSS motifs** — put backdrops as direct children of `<body>`, BEFORE `.stage` (content sits above):
- `<div class="bg-stars"></div>` — a deterministic starfield.
- `<div class="bg-glow blue" style="width:640px;height:640px;top:-120px;right:-120px"></div>` — a soft accent glow (position + size inline).
- `<div class="ghost">165</div>` — an oversized faint number behind the content.
- `<span class="grad-text">…</span>` — gradient accent text.
- Motion (seekable, paused): `class="float"` — a slow one-shot upward drift from +26px to rest
  (NOT a loop/bob); distinct from `class="reveal-up"` which is a 48px entrance + fade. Use `.float`
  for atmospheric elements that settle into position; use `.reveal-up` for content entrances.

**Inline SVG motifs** (copy-paste; style with `fill`/`stroke`/`.float`/`.draw`):
```html
<!-- generic rocket silhouette -->
<svg width="180" height="320" viewBox="0 0 60 120" class="float" style="position:absolute;right:160px;top:300px;z-index:1">
  <path d="M30 4 C42 22 44 52 44 78 H16 C16 52 18 22 30 4 Z" fill="var(--blue)"/>
  <path d="M16 78 L4 104 L18 92 Z M44 78 L56 104 L42 92 Z" fill="var(--orange)"/>
  <circle cx="30" cy="46" r="7" fill="var(--bg)"/>
</svg>
<!-- orbit ring (use .draw for a stroke-on; path/circle must set pathLength="1") -->
<svg width="520" height="520" viewBox="0 0 200 200" style="position:absolute;left:-80px;bottom:-120px;z-index:1;opacity:.5">
  <circle cx="100" cy="100" r="90" fill="none" stroke="var(--surface)" stroke-width="2" pathLength="1" class="draw"/>
</svg>
```

**Pictures (`gpt-image` backdrops or your own photos)** — a LOCAL image is allowed (a `file://`
path is offline/deterministic; only NETWORK assets are forbidden). Use it as a darkened backdrop:
```html
<img class="bg-photo" src="file:///ABS/PATH/assets/bg_01.png" alt="">
<div class="scrim"></div>
<div class="stage"><!-- legible text over the photo --></div>
```
A gpt-image backdrop must stay **generic/atmospheric** (`broll`) — no fabricated specific
vehicle/event/figure, no embedded numbers — the facts live in the page text, never in the image.

## Soft AI backgrounds + glass cards (depth without clutter)
To give a designed deck more depth, place a **generic, atmospheric AI image** (a `broll` —
no logos/text/specific subjects) BEHIND the content at low opacity, and put the real content in
**translucent "glass" cards** so the backdrop reads *through* the blocks instead of being fully
covered. Keep it subtle — the image adds atmosphere, the text still carries every fact.

- **Per-page soft backdrop:** first child of `<body>`, then a tint for palette cohesion:
  ```html
  <img class="bg-soft" src="file:///ABS/OUT_DIR/.assets/<hash>.png" alt="" style="opacity:.14">
  <div class="bg-soft-tint"></div>
  ```
  Tune `opacity` inline: **content/middle pages ~.12–.18**; the **atmospheric opener & closer ends
  ~.34–.46** (more image-forward, since those beats are sparse). One or two reused textures across
  the middle pages keep it cohesive and cheap — you do NOT need a distinct image per page.
- **Glass cards:** add `glass` to any `.card` so the backdrop shows through:
  `<div class="card glass">…</div>`. The translucency is an alpha fill (renders under the
  `--disable-gpu` screenshot path); the `backdrop-filter` blur is a bonus that may be ignored.
- **Faithfulness:** the soft image is decorative `broll` only — generic/atmospheric, never a
  specific vehicle/person/logo and never embedded text or numbers. Facts stay in the card text.
- **Generate the images** with `imagegen` (the same provider as the rest of the tier): Codex
  (`imagegen._generate_codex(prompt, out_path)`, no key) when the `codex` CLI is present, else the
  OpenAI key path (`imagegen.generate(prompt, out_path, key)`); reference the cached file by
  `file://`. Per-page AI imagery is **opt-in** (it costs time/credits) — present the prompts and
  get sign-off before generating, exactly like the non-HTML gpt-image tier.

## SVG icons (category marks, used with restraint) — see `references/icons.md`
Inline-SVG line icons (one coherent Lucide family, themeable via `currentColor`) can mark a row of
**category / feature cards** or flag status. Use the `.icon-tile` / `.icon-badge` / `.icon` classes
(in `motifs.css`) and paste a glyph from `references/icons.md`. Discipline (enforced by `critic-content`):
an icon must do a JOB (answer *what is this / what does it do / why care*) — never decoration; ONE
family; **semantic fit**; color-code a category row by setting `color:` per tile; keep the text label;
≤ the title size; and **no icon on an evidence/stat beat** (a `chart`/number/figure is the focal
point). A few, consistent, purposeful — not one on every page.

## Theming (topic-fitting color)
Link the stylesheets in THIS order: `base.css` → **`theme.css`** → `motifs.css`. `theme.css` is
written by `scripts/theme.py <out_dir>` (it samples `frames/` for a curated light/dark palette, or
takes `--mode/--accent/--bg` for a topic palette) and overrides the `:root` vars. **Author pages
with the semantic vars only** — `var(--bg) var(--surface) var(--fg) var(--muted) var(--accent)
var(--accent2) var(--rule) var(--scrim) var(--on-accent)` (older `var(--blue)/var(--orange)` still
alias to the accents). Never hardcode a hex in a page — that's how a page goes off-theme.

## Illustrated content page (image + Ken-Burns)
A content beat with `media` becomes a two-column `.split` page: text on one side, an image panel on
the other. The side image is held **STATIC** — a zooming image next to revealing bullets is
distracting (and steps with the cue capture). Ken-Burns is reserved for full-bleed hero `.bg-photo`
backdrops; inside a `.split` it's disabled by `.split .media img{animation:none}`.
```html
<div class="split">
  <div><div class="kicker reveal">SECTION</div>
    <div class="title reveal-up" style="animation-delay:.1s">Headline</div>
    <div class="grid" style="margin-top:28px;gap:22px">
      <div class="row reveal-up" style="animation-delay:.3s"><span class="dot"></span><span class="label">Point</span></div>
    </div></div>
  <div class="media"><img class="kenburns" src="file:///ABS/OUT_DIR/.assets/<hash>.png" alt=""></div>
</div>
```
The `src` is the storyboard's `slide.image` value (imagegen caches under `.assets/<hash>.png`),
referenced as `file://<out_dir>/<slide.image>`. Do NOT use a literal `assets/scene_NN.png` path.
The image is a generic atmospheric **broll** (generated via `imagegen`); the facts stay as text.
Only CSS animation (`.kenburns` + reveals) — no JS-timed motion, no network assets — so `seek.js`
captures it deterministically.

## Typographic roles (use the named classes — never a raw font-size)
`.stat` = a single data value · `.title` = the primary claim · `.sub` = supporting context (always
`--muted`) · `.kicker` = a category label (mono, accent-coloured) · `.note` = secondary annotation. Keep
the hierarchy contract: `.title`/`.sub` ≥ 2.5×, `.title`/`.note` ≥ 3×. (`var(--blue)`/`var(--orange)`
are semantic *accent aliases*, not hardcoded colours — using them is fine; a literal `#rrggbb` is not.)

## Layout diversity — no samey deck (enforced)
Across the deck's `html` scenes, **no single form family may exceed ~45%**. A deck that is card/row
grids top to bottom reads as auto-generated — the exact "AI slop" this tier exists to avoid. If you're
reaching for a card grid a third time, STOP and re-read the form-selection table above: the content
almost always wants a `.flow` / `.scorecard` / `.quadrant` / `.timeline` / `.hubspoke` / `.segbar`
instead. `validate.py` counts the families and warns when one dominates; `critic-content` (R8) fails it.

## Composition helpers (pair with the forms above)
- **`.card`** — a panel with depth (`--surface` + shadow + hairline); group related rows. **`.card.glass`** over a soft backdrop.
- **`.dash`** (3-up) / **`.grid-asym`** (2fr 1fr) — dashboard + asymmetric layouts; break the centred-column monotony.
- **`.defocus`** — on a comparison, add to the NON-focal side for depth-of-field (subtle blur, not flat dim).
- **`.accent-fill`** — on `<body>` of a section-divider beat: full-bleed accent background, `--on-accent` text.
- **`.reveal-pop`** — spring overshoot for a hero `.stat`/`.num`. **`.reveal-up-sm`** — shorter rise for dense sub-items.
- **`.chrome`** — a mono SECTION-LABEL rail (direct child of `<body>`); reuse the section/topic name across beats as a quiet editorial through-line. **NOT a page number / progress bar / counter** (that's the banned player-chrome — a video has nothing to navigate).

## Reveal timing — points must NOT lead the voice (important)
The most common defect is **content appearing well before the narration reaches it**. Avoid it:
- **Multi-point content pages SHOULD be audio-synced with `data-cue`** (see "Audio-synced reveals"
  below) — the precise *and* efficient path: each point reveals exactly when its spoken anchor is
  heard, and the renderer only screenshots around each cue. Make this the default for any page with
  ≥2 content points; the content-planner emits a per-beat `cue` array to support it.
- **If a page is NOT cued, leave `anim_seconds` UNSET** on content pages — the renderer defaults it to
  spread the reveals across ~70% of the scene (tracking the speaking pace) instead of cramming them into
  the first second. Set `anim_seconds` explicitly only for heroes/title pages (~1.2–1.5s) or to override.
  Do NOT set a small `anim_seconds` (2–3s) on a long (10s+) content page — every point flashes in early
  and the rest of the scene is static. **`validate.py` warns** when an uncued multi-point page has an
  `anim_seconds` < half the scene; **`critic-content` (R2) also flags reveals that lead the audio.**

## Stagger cadence (seek-safe)
- **Header chrome** (kicker → rule → title → sub) appears fast: `0s`, `.05s`, `.10s`, `.25s`.
- **Content POINTS appear one-by-one** — NOT all at once. Stagger rows/cards with `.reveal-up-sm`
  (first `~.4s`, then `~+.5s` per point). With `data-cue` the real reveal time comes from the audio
  (these inline delays are ignored); without cues the paced spread above applies.
- **Equal-height cards:** rows of cards (`.dash`) are equal height by design (`align-items:stretch`); do
  not set per-card heights. If one card's text is much longer, shorten it or move it to its own beat.
- **Audio-synced cues override stagger:** when audio-synced cues are active (edge-tts + `data-cue`
  attributes), `seek.js` overrides each cued point's delay with its resolved cue time from
  `audio/NN.words.json`; your stagger `animation-delay` values on cued points are ignored.

## One-concept rule + whitespace floor
ONE primary per page (a stat OR a list OR a chart — not two stacked). Content must not fill more than
~60% of the canvas; if a row grid overflows below 960px, SPLIT the beat — never shrink `.stage` padding below 80px.

## Anti-slop checklist (do NOT)
emoji in titles · full-screen purple/pink/blue gradient-mesh backgrounds · circle+left-border accent
cards (use `.card`/`.row`) · SVG depicting realistic scenes/figures · decorative bottom progress bars /
timecodes / chapter counters (player-chrome) · hardcoded hex (use semantic vars) · network/CDN links.

## Pre-render checklist
absolute `file://` paths (files exist) · no `<link href="http…">` · base.css → theme.css → motifs.css
linked · no content overflow below 960px · semantic vars only · all `.reveal*`/`.kenburns` keep
`animation-play-state:paused` · no leftover debug overlays.

## Audio-synced reveals (points appear when spoken)
On a multi-point page, tag each point's reveal element with `data-cue-index="0|1|2…"` (in SPOKEN
order) and `data-cue="<the spoken anchor phrase>"` — the word/phrase in the narration that introduces
that point (usually the point's keyword; set it to a different phrase only when the visible label is
not spoken verbatim). Example:
```html
<div class="row reveal-up-sm" data-cue-index="0" data-cue="Dujiangyan"> … </div>
<div class="row reveal-up-sm" data-cue-index="1" data-cue="Leshan"> … </div>
```
When edge-tts word timings exist (`audio/NN.words.json`), `render_html` reveals each point exactly when
its anchor is spoken (across the whole scene). With no word timings (macOS `say`, or a missing anchor)
it falls back to the paced `anim_seconds` stagger. Heroes/title pages don't use `data-cue`. The anchor
must be a phrase actually present in that scene's narration.

> ⚠️ **Cued pages capture only the header window + cue bursts.** On a cued page, `render_html`
> shoots fresh frames during the initial header window (~1.2s) and around each cue, and HOLDS
> (copies) elsewhere. So a NON-cued element with a long animation freezes partway: `.float` (3s)
> and `.draw` (1.4s) won't finish. On a cued page, keep non-cued decorative motion short
> (≤ ~1.2s) or give those elements a `data-cue` so they're captured. Plain `.reveal*` header
> chrome is fine (it settles by ~1s).
